thread:
maria: FYI getting multiple customer reports about P99 spikes on text-generation endpoints since the 04:00 deploy. p95 okay-ish but p99 up ~3x. seeing heat across eu-west and us-central.

sahil: ack. Is this limited to a single model or across variants? any error rates?

maria: mostly gptx-compat-3.1 and gptx-3-small-prod. error rates minimal (2xx), but tails are long. traces show a lot of time in 'kv_lookup' and 'prefix_cache.get'.

ryan: @maria can you paste a trace? also which commit rolled at 04:00?

maria: here’s a representative trace dump: ```
span: request 0 -> 1.2s
  - routing: 8ms
  - model_load: 30ms
  - kv_lookup(prefix=\"user:pref:1234\"): 980ms
  - kv_store.write: 5ms
  - decode: 150ms
```

kelsey: weird that kv_lookup is blocking that long. infra metrics show prefix_cache miss rate jumped from 2% -> 65% at 04:03. eviction_count spiked too.

infra-bot: deploy-bot deployed commit 6f9a2b to prod at 04:00:12 (redwood/runtime#4123).

maria: suspect a cache key change in that commit. the new keygen added user-session-id into prefix key which exploded cardinality.

sahil: confirmed in code: `prefix_key = f\"{user_id}:{session_id}:{prefix}\"` — session_id is high-cardinality. previous impl used `user_id:prefix`.

ryan: that would cause cache thrash. small cache + higher cardinality -> constant evictions, warmup fails -> p99. any quick mitigations?

kelsey: we can hotfix to roll back keygen in runtime (re-add session_id only for tracing, not cache key). but symmetric issue: many warmed entries are now useless. need to warm critical prefixes.

maria: immediate mitigation plan: 1) rollback runtime keygen to previous commit (safe, small diff). 2) bump prefix_cache.size from 50k -> 200k for 2 hours to reduce eviction churn. 3) run a warmup task to populate top-100 prefixes for heavy customers. 4) add telemetry to detect high-cardinality keys.

sahil: agree. rolling back now would stop new crazy keys but won't restore cache state. bumping cache size is quick (flag in config), warmup script is in infra/playbooks/warmup-prefixes.

ryan: I'm on rollback PR. @kelsey can you patch config to increase cache size and start warmup? also add a temporary metric `prefix_cardinality_rate` so we can alert next time.

kelsey: on it. patching config in config-service now. example snippet to change: ```yaml
prefix_cache:
  size: 200000
  eviction_policy: LRU
```

maria: also adding a short-circuit in prefix_cache.get: if key looks like `.*:sessionid:.*` treat it as non-cacheable to avoid future regressions until we fix keygen validation. will push to canary after rollback.

infra-bot: config-service change queued, will apply to prod pool in ~90s.

deploy-bot: rollback PR 6f9a2b -> 4a3c19 merged by ryan at 04:12:05.

kelsey: warmup started for top-100 prefixes (parallel workers=20). script logs at /var/logs/warmup-prefixes/1815501234.log.

maria: after applying both changes (rollback + cache bump) we should see miss rate drop. watching dashboards.

sahil: quick note for postmortem: add a unit test that asserts cache_key cardinality change < 2x across a simulated user population, and a lint that flags inclusion of session IDs in cache keys.

ryan: agreed. also add a chaos test where we simulate spikey session ids to ensure eviction_count doesn't blow out.

kelsey: metrics update: at 04:18 miss_rate is down from 65% -> 12%, eviction_count trending down, p99 latency decreased from 1.9s -> 320ms on the canary cluster. prod trailing but following.

maria: customers notified via support: #support-ticket-3492 updated. cc @oncall-support.

sahil: long-term followups: - tighter cache key review in PR checklist - add cardinality guardrails on config UI - add auto-warm for top prefixes after deploys - telemetry to alert when miss_rate > 20% and eviction spike > 3x baseline.

maria: I'll draft the incident blameless postmortem. thanks all for quick reaction. :tada: 

ryan: nice teamwork. one action item assigned: ryan -> rollback/PR; kelsey -> config/warmup; sahil -> tests/alerting; maria -> postmortem & customer comms. closing thread once postmortem linked.

deploy-bot: release note: rollback applied, config bump applied (temp).

maria: leaving a follow-up link to the postmortem draft: https://redwood.internal/pm/postmortems/kv-cache-thrash-1815501234 (will update).

kelsey: closing monitoring loop, will keep watch for 2h and then revert temp cache bump to original size.

maria: thanks everyone.
